There were the usual caveats in the jobs report as education and hospitality added much of the gains but overall it was still a strong report.

The big retracement in the dollar was more about Fed thinking, with Waller yesterday indicating that the jobs report wouldn't be a big factor in his thinking.

Still, the implied odds of a hike moved to 58% from 49% and short-dated yields rose 4 bps.

The yen remained in focus and there were fresh signs of meddling as the pair fell more than 200 pips from the post-NFP jump.

After reaching 155.40 the pair climbed steadily back to 156.26 to finish the day up around 50 pips.
